identity: Social reformer and writer · United Kingdom · 1838–1912
title: Octavia Hill's birth chart
metaDescription: Octavia Hill's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 10.9° Sagittarius. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: Four of the ten placements whose signs are settled stand in Sagittarius — the Sun, Mercury, Venus and Saturn. The placements whose signs could change with an unknown hour are not counted. A cluster that size becomes the section the rest of the chart plays around.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: Measured rather than labelled, the Sun holds 10.9° Sagittarius: the second decan, whose classical sub-ruler is Mars. A fire sign, read here in its second face.

blocks.title: The fast planets
blocks.text: Mercury holds 26.6° Sagittarius, Venus holds 7.3° Sagittarius, Mars holds 14.3° Virgo — in the old shorthand, a mind that decides at speaking speed; taste that runs toward the vivid and the immediate; drive that grinds rather than flares.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: Venus to Neptune is the closest call of the day, a sextile within 0.9°. A sextile is an offer rather than a given: available when it is reached for, quiet when it is not. Behind it, Venus square Uranus at 1.4°, and the Sun square Uranus at 2.3° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. Each angle here was measured at every hour of the civil day and held; whatever the missing clock said, this geometry was in it.

blocks.title: What the angles build
blocks.text: Mars opposes Uranus while both square the Sun. The t-square is the figure the old texts trusted for output: friction with a fixed address. The Moon stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Of the seven planets the classical scheme judges, two sit in a sign it has an opinion about. The Moon in Cancer at 7.3° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules; Mercury in Sagittarius at 26.6° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain. Condition, not character: that is all the dignity table ever measured.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Counting only the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the chart runs 5 fire, 2 water, 2 air, 1 earth by element and 6 mutable, 3 cardinal, 1 fixed by modality. Pluto was retrograde — apparent retreat against the stars, which the old reading takes as a function working from the inside first.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Cancer for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 13.7° between midnight and midnight. Fast enough that its degree is approximate, slow enough that its sign is not in doubt. At the noon reference it stands at 7.3°.
